text:
rachael: Heads-up — coordinated base-image rebuild + cosign KMS signer rotation tonight 23:00 UTC. Scope: runtime nodes (userns + minimal rootfs), vulns patched (glibc), and rotate signer key. Need RBAC review, audit-sink checks, and canary plan. Who can take RBAC and audit ownership?

anil: I can own RBAC. What exact permissions do we want for the signer SA?

rachael: For the cosign signer service account we plan to grant minimal perms:
```
roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier
roles/storage.objectViewer
roles/iam.serviceAccountUser
```
We'll create a new SA cosign-signer@redwood-infra and limit membership to the build pipeline only. Also, we intend to rotate the KMS key to a new key version at start of window.

mariya: Audit logs checklist: export KMS cryptoOperations and IAM POLICY_CHANGE to security-project BigQuery sink, and ensure containerd/cosign events from runtime nodes route to the same sink. Ops, can you confirm logforwarder has the new filters?

security-oncall: Note — RBAC change requires sec-leads approval before +30m of rollout, I'll open approval ticket now. Also flag: prior base image had glibc CVE-2026-XYZ unfixed; ensure patched image passes vuln scan before canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled rebuild job queued: job-id=abc123, start=2026-03-21T23:00:00Z, target=runtime-pool, canary=5%

leila: For canary, recommend us-west1 only, 5% of fleet, block egress to prod KMS until cosign verify passes. If verify OK, promote egress to prod KMS for next wave.

anil: RBAC binding snippet I'll apply once approved: 
```yaml
- role: roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier
  members:
  - serviceAccount:cosign-signer@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
I'll lock binding to the keyring resource.

mariya: Also create a log metric for cosign.verify.errors and route to pager. We want a threshold alert: >3 errors in 5m during canary. Export key usage to audit table for postmortem.

pat: I'll run vuln triage for the window. Plan: run internal vuln-scan on canaries post-start, and run exploit repro for criticals. If any vuln severity >= 9 or active exploit reproducible, we stop rollout.

ops-bot: canary started: instances: us-west1-n1-{i-23,i-24,i-25}, job-id=abc123, stage=canary, started=2026-03-21T23:05:00Z

[log] 2026-03-21T23:05:12Z cosign[verify] ERROR: signature verification failed for image runtime/base:sha256:6f3a...

anil: If that pops up check KMS key version and IAM allowlist. Command: `gcloud kms keys versions list --key=cosign-key --keyring=infra-rk --location=global`

rachael: If signature failures >3 in 5m, auto-rollback the image and abort key rotation. Patch plan: revert to previous signed image and open incident.

security-oncall: I'll watch audit stream and approve rollback if I see anomalous cryptoOperations or policy changes. Setting a temporary watch in the console and will escalate if unusual access from unknown IP ranges. :eyes:

pat: Canaries currently running vuln-scan (baseline + glibc checks). Will post scan output in 10m.

ops-bot: canary scan complete: vulns found: glibc CVE-2026-XYZ -> fixed in current rebuilt image (score 7.5). No criticals.

rachael: Good. After 30m stable canary we'll roll 20% -> 50% -> 100% in 20m steps with 5m stabilization between each. All rollouts gated by cosign.verify.errors and vuln-scan pass.

security-oncall: Add post-rollout audit tasks: snapshot KMS key access logs, export verification metric, and attach to PM for postmortem. I'll create the checklist in the approval ticket.

anil: Applying IAM binding once approval comes through. Will limit `iam.serviceAccountUser` to the build pipeline SA only.

rachael: Thanks — I'll kick off ticket for sec-leads and post final plan here. If anyone wants to be on the incident channel for the window ping me and I'll add you. :thumbsup:

pat: Adding notes — will capture vuln-scan artifacts and attach them to the rollout ticket for traceability.

rachael: Closing loop: if anything goes sideways open an incident in #incidents and tag @security-oncall and @eng-oncall. I'll update postmortem if we hit any failures.

security-oncall: Roger. Monitoring now.
